# Architecture Heuristics

This document records accepted, cross-cutting decision guidance for RelayView.
Heuristics are defaults for evaluating new designs; they are neither domain
vocabulary nor claims that a behavior has been implemented. A design may depart
from a heuristic when it records the concrete invariant, limitation, or evidence
that requires the exception. A consequential, hard-to-reverse exception may
also require an architecture decision record.

Verified current behavior remains documented in the relevant authoritative
subsystem contract. Specific consequential decisions and their tradeoffs remain
documented in `docs/authoritative/adr/`. The form those documents take — present
tense, contract rather than changelog, and which issue references are retained —
is governed by [authoritative documentation standards](authoritative-documentation-standards.md),
not by a heuristic here. The accepted owner decisions below are one of the
reference categories that document retains.

## Optimize For Human Attention And Direction

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-19: treat human attention and direction as the
scarce resources in agent-assisted development. RelayView's objective is to turn
human intent into verified, useful outcomes with less supervision and decision
overhead. Producing more code is not sufficient evidence of progress toward that
objective.

Use clear contracts, deterministic tools, and admitted automated validation and
review to handle work that otherwise demands repeated human checking and
correction. Preserve human direction over goals, scope, consequential tradeoffs,
and acceptance. Make intervention useful: present the decision needed, the
relevant evidence, uncertainty, and consequences without requiring the person
to reconstruct the execution history. Routine coordination and repeated
explanations should not consume attention that the system can conserve.

The existing [automated review workflow](planner-review-rounds.md) and the planned
Human Review Brief serve this objective through different responsibilities:
automated review can identify defects before Human review, while the brief is
intended to organize the exact candidate, checks, unresolved concerns, and
decision context for efficient inspection. The brief remains roadmap work;
neither mechanism's existence proves a reduction in human effort.

Evaluate active supervision and review time, avoidable interruptions, repeated
instructions, decision quality, and subsequent rework alongside coding outcomes,
latency, and resource use. Preserve visibility of uncertainty and required
acceptance boundaries while reducing burden. The
[human-decision hypothesis](../speculative/relayview-theory-of-effectiveness.md#h6-inspectable-evidence-can-improve-human-decisions-if-it-reduces-review-burden)
records the expected benefit and evidence limits. This is a product design
priority, not a claim that model capability, correctness, or compute constraints
have ceased to matter.

### Design For Sustained Work Between Human Checkpoints

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-20: design RelayView for long periods of useful
work without routine human input, including overnight runs. Preconfiguration
enables unattended execution, which serves the broader objective of conserving
human attention. This principle applies across Community and Teams.

Owner decision, accepted 2026-10-04: concentrate necessary Human interaction
into deliberate checkpoints that unlock the longest safe interval of independent
work. Ask foreseeable questions as soon as there is enough evidence to answer
them reliably, and collect related questions, setup steps, and requests for new
authority into one useful checkpoint. Optimize the number and timing of
interruptions as well as total Human effort. Do not ask speculative questions
that the workflow can resolve within its existing authority merely to make a
checkpoint look complete.

Move foreseeable configuration and authorization decisions before execution.
Let users establish task direction, acceptance criteria, supported capabilities,
dependency sources, external-service access, credential bindings, and resource
limits upfront. Within that configured authority, design routine acquisition,
builds, tests, coordination, and bounded recovery to proceed without repeated
user confirmation. Surface detectable missing prerequisites before a run so
users can resolve them while preparing the work.

An agent-ready assignment has no known unresolved consequential choice that
would predictably stop implementation. Task preparation should expose such
choices while a Human is already defining the work; readiness does not promise
that unexpected questions will never arise. Collaborative task preparation and
unattended implementation are separate interactions. Their overlap lets a Human
shape future tasks while ready tasks continue through owner-controlled roles.

When execution encounters a consequential decision, missing configuration, or a
need for new authority, preserve progress and continue independent authorized
work where possible. Before interrupting the Human, examine other foreseeable
decisions needed to resume useful work and present the related questions together
with their evidence, options, and consequences. Leave a clear account of any
remaining blocker; do not invent permission or count blocked verification as
passed. Prepare results and verification evidence for human inspection, manual
testing, acceptance, and further direction.

The first safe opportunity to interact with an exact implementation candidate
is another useful Human checkpoint. Make that candidate inspectable and, where
practical, manually testable so the Human can discover defects or differences
from their intent before merge. Formal approval still follows the required
current verification and review evidence, and applies only to the candidate
actually inspected. A changed candidate needs fresh applicable evidence and a
fresh Human decision. This checkpoint is part of conserving attention:
discovering an intent mismatch before merge avoids a later interruption and
repair cycle.

Make the review package especially usable for intermediate changes whose value
is not obvious from a visible feature. Explain why the change matters, identify
the exact candidate, and separate what current deterministic checks establish
from what they cannot assess. A bounded contract with enumerable inputs and
outputs may have strong automated coverage and little value in repeating the
same calls by hand. Interface clarity, visual layout, discoverability, and fit
to Human intent often need direct inspection even when focused browser tests
pass; expanding brittle browser assertions cannot exhaust those judgments.

State the remaining Human review need explicitly. When direct exercise can
resolve it, give the shortest repeatable setup, action, and expected observation
for the exact candidate. When manual testing adds little, say why the automated
evidence is a suitable basis for the Human's decision and name its limits; do
not create busywork to fill a checklist. When useful manual testing is
impractical, explain the constraint without implying that the Human exercised
the behavior. Human acceptance remains necessary in every case, and neither
automated coverage nor a successful manual check is proof beyond its stated
scope.

unattended work is accepted design guidance; whether this rhythm reduces total
human effort remains a hypothesis, and this principle does not establish that
every supporting capability is implemented.

# Bounded shared research MCP

`@relayview/research-mcp` is at version 1.3.0 under `src/research/mcp/`.
It compiles the [shared core](reusable-research-core.md) source into its standalone
tarball; there is no copied ranker or OpenCode fork. Core API 1/package 1.3.0 and
`lexical-v2-initial-4` retain four initial structural chunks, three explicitly
requested continuation chunks, eight continuations and exact cumulative 120 KiB
document accounting. It performs no semantic inference and no multi-source retrieval.

## Transport and authority

Native clients launch `bridge.js` using MCP stdio. It connects only to a local
Unix socket. A separately supervised `main.js` owns the engine and one immutable
trusted session, policy, work ledger and cache namespace. The bridge has no
provider, policy, budget or credential options; changing tool arguments cannot
change trusted service identity. The standalone host has no persistent search
cache; a trusted embedding host may use the core's separately namespaced cache.

## Source-profile activation

With no source option, `main.js` derives `public-web-v1`; GitHub search records
and fetches remain allowed. `--github-excluded` derives `github-excluded-v1` and
its exact five-family canonical exclusion descriptor. The option is trusted
service configuration, never an MCP tool argument. Unknown or duplicated options
and a setup policy already bound to a conflicting profile fail before readiness.

Readiness contains `sourcePolicy.requestedProfileId` and the complete effective
descriptor. The effective semantic policy hash, setup digest, compact evidence,
cache/flight identity, transient continuation identity, and MCP/core release bind
the same descriptor. The exclusion path returns typed `source_forbidden` denials;
it does not retry or fall back. See
[Reusable lexical research core](reusable-research-core.md#versioned-source-profiles)
for domain matching, search filtering, redirect handling, cache v2, and preserved
SSRF/accounting behavior.

The supervisor supplies version-1 setup JSON through inherited descriptor 3,
and the Brave credential through descriptor 4, each bounded and closed after
bootstrap (16 KiB/4 KiB, five-second waits). Public stdin is never a setup channel.
The setup object contains exactly `contractVersion`, `sessionId`,
`capabilityIdentity`, `cacheNamespace`, `policy` (the core's `CorePolicy`) and
`limits` (core work dimensions). The core validates its policy and logical-call
ceiling; `limits.calls` is also the service call limit. There is no benchmark
numeric default. Config, credentials and control descriptors belong outside
agent workspaces and environments. Only allowlisted compact evidence goes to
the supervisor's stderr; readiness on its private stdout includes release,
policy and setup digest. Ready means transport setup, **not live availability**.
Readiness also reports the requested and complete effective source policy.

The socket is mode 0600 in an existing supervisor-owned mode-0700 directory.
Each client sees only its assigned socket through a read-only mount and immutable
client configuration/bridge binaries. The directory/socket mount is a capability,
not a bearer token or a model-selectable session selector. The supervisor must
hide all other trial sockets, credentials, retained setup and writable service
paths from agent commands. Same-UID unrestricted host access can replace or
connect to such resources and is **not contained by Unix modes**. Benchmark
namespace provisioning, resource cgroups and durable recovery are owned by the
separate `agent-harness-evals` repository; this package proves the network-disabled bridge topology, not
complete benchmark containment. Model-provider routes are owned by the native harness configuration.

## Wire and failure contract

The adapter supports MCP revisions 2024-11-05, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25, using
newline-delimited UTF-8 JSON-RPC. Unknown revisions negotiate 2025-06-18. Initialize,
initialized notification, ping, tools/list, tools/call and cancellation are the
only methods; resources, prompts, control, dynamic tools and batching are absent.
The tool inventory is exactly `web_search`, `web_fetch`, and `youtube_transcript`. Fetch has the core's
initial or explicit continuation input, not an automatic follow-up loop. The
fetch description states that public PDF documents are extracted to bounded
untrusted text under an admitting policy and that encrypted or scanned PDFs
return `encrypted_document` and `textless_document`. The transcript tool takes
a bounded video reference with an optional simple language tag; its description
states the manual-over-generated preference and the `captions_unavailable`
outcome for missing, disabled, or private captions.

Each result has one `content` text block: the canonical core result plus
`untrusted: true`. `structuredContent` is absent. Canonical JSON is limited to
128 KiB in UTF-8; the full MCP response is independently limited to 1 MiB,
below Pi's separate 1.25 MiB adapter ceiling. Escaping is measured after
serialization. Oversized success becomes a typed error, never clipped content.
Core/Pi/MCP goldens preserve content, order, digest, outline, omission metadata,
policy identity and accounting; transport timing and random handles are transient.

Each connection admits at most four pending operations and 8,192 frames, with
16 KiB per frame and a bounded two-response write queue. At most four connections
are active per sidecar. Duplicate JSON-RPC IDs are rejected within a connection;
private core call IDs are generated by the adapter. Reconnect IDs are new calls,
not replay tokens. Core's 4,096-result retention ceiling and ledger limits still
apply across connections. Flooding cannot grow unbounded pending work or buffers.
Oversized frames and exhausted frame allowances abort pending work and flush a
typed error before destroying the connection; a one-second grace timer forces
destruction if writes stall. A peer that leaves its write half open cannot
retain a rejected connection slot.

| Condition | Result/recovery |
| --- | --- |
| No lexical match | Successful empty selection; bounded outline permits explicit continuation. |
| Malformed/unknown research arguments, authority injection | Core `invalid_request`; authorized invalid calls retain core charging. |
| Forbidden preferred domain, direct source, or redirect target | Core `source_forbidden` denial; no fallback or blocked-source delivery. |
| Missing/unknown tool or control method | JSON-RPC `invalid_tool` / `method_not_found`; no research work. |
| Invalid UTF-8/JSON, oversized frame | `invalid_json` / `oversized_request`; oversized connection closes. |
| Duplicate ID / concurrent-call ceiling | `duplicate_request_id` / `concurrency_exhausted`; no new core call. |
| Malformed/oversized adapter result | `malformed_response` / `oversized_response`; no partial success. |
| Logical or internal work exhaustion | Core `budget_exhausted`; no allowance reset or automatic retry. |
| MCP cancellation / service deadline | Core `timeout`; pending work aborts, uncertain reservations remain charged. |
| Bridge/client disconnect | Aborts that connection's work; client observes transport closure. Late results are suppressed. |
| Another session's handle / lost document | Core `document_unavailable`; refetch only under remaining allowance, optionally with expected digest. |
| Service restart | Existing `started` marker refuses launch; never silently restore a fresh volatile allowance. |

The marker is created exclusively and synchronized before listen. It remains
after graceful shutdown or crash. Bridge reconnect to the **same live service**
preserves allowance and transient handles. Service loss ends this standalone
trial: preserve evidence and marker; do not remove it to resume. A separately
authorized new trial requires a fresh directory and identity. Durable accounting
for the production owner is implemented in [owner-research-trials.md](owner-research-trials.md); standalone external provisioning is owned by the separate `agent-harness-evals` repository. The package's embedding API
accepts a trusted `ResearchService`; it does not certify a custom durable ledger.

The same packaged smoke accepts `--live` only inside a trusted systemd service
with `LoadCredentialEncrypted`. It passes the credential's open descriptor to
the service; the network-disabled bridge receives a sanitized environment and
no setup/credential descriptor. The probe performs one Brave query, one public
Node HTTPS documentation fetch, and one three-chunk continuation. With
`--github-excluded` it additionally proves that a forbidden preferred search
domain, direct GitHub fetch and allowed-origin redirect to GitHub all return
`source_forbidden` without delivering blocked content. Its standalone smoke
policy permits exactly three logical calls for the public profile or six for the
GitHub-excluded profile (not benchmark limits).
It prints counts, digest, policy/release and allowance only, never keys/pages.

Prerequisites: an enrolled root-controlled credential at
`/etc/credstore.encrypted/relayview-brave-search-api`, working sudo/systemd,
Node and Bubblewrap; allow one paid Brave search. From the checkout root:

```zsh
npm run build --prefix src/research/mcp
sudo systemd-run --wait --pipe --collect \
  --unit="relayview-mcp-live-$(date +%s)" \
  --property="User=$(id -un)" \
  --property=LoadCredentialEncrypted=relayview-brave-search-api:/etc/credstore.encrypted/relayview-brave-search-api \
  "$(command -v node)" "$(pwd)/src/research/mcp/dist/mcp/smoke.js" --live --github-excluded
```

Expected: zero exit and `live_brave_search_public_fetch`, positive search count,
four/three chunks, three `source_forbidden` denial results, six used calls and
zero remaining. Missing/expired credentials,
provider rejection, network failures, changed source structure or insufficient
remaining outline chunks stop the smoke. Preserve printed diagnostics/marker;
never record readiness or fixture success as live verification. Repair the
operator credential/network condition before starting a separately identified
smoke; do not retry an uncertain trial automatically.

**Live status in this implementation environment:** not run. The enrolled
credential is root-controlled and noninteractive sudo requires a password.
Deterministic/native fixture success does not replace this opt-in check or the
exact five-arm provider-route admission owned by the separate
`agent-harness-evals` repository.

For standalone service recovery, stop the client/bridge, terminate the sidecar,
retain compact evidence and the `started` marker, and mark that trial interrupted.
Do not relaunch into fresh state under the old identity. Rollback selects the
whole prior admitted MCP/core artifact for a new authorized trial, not a mixture
of wrapper and core files. After a disposable trial is conclusively ended and
its diagnostics retained, the supervisor may remove only its exact trial directory.

## Limitations

Production owner and durable trial integration is documented in
[owner-research-trials.md](owner-research-trials.md). Consumer harness migration,
live admission, and benchmark resource sizing are separate work owned outside this
package.

# Owner research trial allowances

A research trial is an explicit research assignment for one owner-managed workflow.
Ordinary sessions keep their immutable per-session policy, budget and automatic
provider-recovery behavior. A trial instead uses the shared `ResearchService`
trusted-host interface and a SQLite `WorkLedger`, across all of its planner and
implementer sessions. It is the research integration that benchmark exports consume;
it is not an admitted comparative benchmark or a complete workflow
scheduler/deadline implementation.

## Assignment and admission

An authenticated interactive owner client sends `research_trial.prepare` before
`workflow.start`. The definition reserves a unique trial ID and workflow command
ID. Workflow creation binds the task in the same transaction that creates its
planner. The assignment cannot move to another task or be attached after workflow
creation. Model input and Pi tools cannot prepare or modify it. Session creation,
replacement, reopening and owner recovery resolve the original assignment.
Changing the active research default does not change a trial's pinned policy.
New preparation rejects retired policies; existing assignments remain recoverable.

The strict version-1 definition contains:

- `trialId`, `workflowCommandId`, and the externally frozen `cohortDigest`;
- `artifactDigest`, taken from the running owner's runtime-identity endpoint;
- `policy: {id, version, hash}`, naming an existing immutable research policy;
- all eight `limits` counters listed below, and `roleCallLimits` for planner and
  implementer (use the aggregate call limit when no additional sublimit is wanted);
- an absolute ISO `deadlineAt`, and fixed `networkedOperation: "denied"`,
  `cache: "owner_namespaced"`, `automaticRetries: 0`, `contractVersion: 1`.

`runtime` is reserved and cannot be a trial ID. Numeric limits must be nonnegative safe integers. Calls are capped at 4096;
role sublimits cannot exceed the aggregate. Scoring windows and tokens must be
zero. No benchmark-wide numeric allowance is supplied by this implementation.
The research deadline must be in the future at setup/start. It bounds research
admission and in-flight research, not planning, validation or total task duration.
The external benchmark runner must enforce its separately frozen total deadline.

Runtime identity includes package/selection versions, a digest of the exact core
files, and an owner artifact digest covering research files, accounting/admission
adapters, the dependency lock and effective cache configuration. Source/compiled
runs have distinct identities. Each process captures its identity at startup and
refuses to advertise or admit a rebuilt artifact until restart; hashing changed
files cannot relabel modules already loaded in memory. Preparation, workflow binding, session launch,
recovery and calls reject artifact/policy drift. The private broker independently
checks its artifact against the owner before execution. Export remains readable
after drift and reports `runtimeMatches: false`. A cohort digest is an operator
assertion: the owner does not fetch or validate an external cohort manifest.

Planner/implementer admission requires the research pair and `broker_only`
networking, with the existing bounded role tool inventory. The owner-mediated
focused-Chat publication tool is part of the production Planner, Implementer,
and Reviewer transport and remains admitted; it does not grant research or
network access. The planner inventory also admits `observe_task`; execution
still requires the explicit task-liaison relation and accepted Plan v1 under the
[task-observation contract](planner-task-observation.md). This tool adds no
research or network authority and is rejected in implementer/reviewer inventories.
Workflow reservation validates both prospective assignments
before any planner launch or research; recovery revalidates the frozen
implementer assignment before resuming planning. Reviewers retain their bounded
candidate-read tools, `submit_review_result`, focused-Chat publication, and
offline networking; independent reviewer research is zero. Unsupported
roles/tools fail admission. Trial command execution and
validation reject `networked_operation`; planner work-tracker network operations
are also denied. Preprovision dependencies for restricted validation. Imported
external session history is rejected for trial tasks. Existing owner review,
validation, handoff and completion gates remain in force.

## Accounting and content

Schema 34 adds `research_trial`, `research_trial_call` and
`research_trial_work`. SQLite immediate transactions reserve across all roles;
logical calls, physical effects and reconciliation have stable durable identities.
A replacement session gets no fresh allowance. Each effect records its role,
originating call, maximum and acknowledged actual use. Duplicate reconciliation
must match; it cannot increase work, change a previous actual value, or release
another session's charge.

Counters are `calls`, `providerAttempts`, `fetchedDocuments`, `fetchedBytes`,
`scoringPairs`, `scoringWindows`, `scoringTokens`, and `elapsedMs`.
Their exact units and reservation rules are in
[reusable-research-core.md](reusable-research-core.md#work-reservations-replay-and-lifecycle).
In particular, fetched bytes are decoded body bytes, not network traffic, and
elapsed work is summed execution wall time reserved at the per-call deadline,
not CPU time or total workflow time. Failures/cancellation/unknown outcomes retain
their reserved maximum. Zero confirmed work never means that uncertain work was free.

Before the trial deadline, exact call replay in the running dispatcher returns
its retained result with no new charge. Completed, in-flight and recovered replays
remain subject to the same deadline: expiry returns `timeout` without revealing
retained content, repeating work or overwriting the original evidence. Changed bytes under the same ID are rejected. Replay after restart or
bounded transient-result eviction returns `unavailable` with the original evidence
identity; it never repeats network work or overwrites the original evidence.
An explicit retry uses a new ID and consumes a new admitted call. There is no
automatic provider retry in trials. Trial and ordinary searches share one Brave
adapter, including provider concurrency, start-rate and backoff state. Malformed canonical input consumes an admitted
call; pre-cancellation, offline/unavailable admission and exhausted limits do not
start effects. The core reserves before cache/network/scoring effects. Existing startup provider probes remain owner startup operations outside the trial allowance; benchmark operators must retain their logs and include that overhead in their declared lifecycle.

Cache hits and coalesced waiters each consume a logical call. Only the initiating
scope owns a shared physical provider attempt, even if that caller cancels while
another waiter remains. Policy, provider and trial namespace separate cache entries
and shared flights. Trial caches never fall back to ordinary-session cache keys.
Document handles are transient and scoped to session/capability/policy; another
trial cannot use them. Broker restart loses handles; refetch with a new call ID and
`expectedDocumentDigest` if source identity must remain unchanged.

The pinned lexical release returns up to four initial structural chunks, or three
explicit continuation chunks. Eight continuations and 120 KiB cumulative document
visibility remain the core ceilings. Canonical JSON is bounded at 128 KiB and the
Pi envelope independently at 1.25 MiB. Pi and MCP preserve the same content for
identical input snapshots/policies; opaque handles and expiry times differ by
session. Existing plain-text/HTML/Markdown/JSON/XML normalization and public HTTPS
restrictions remain unchanged. A policy carrying the `pdfExtraction` admission
also extracts bounded text from public PDF documents through the same `web_fetch`
boundary. There is no image, audio, semantic-inference or
multi-source retrieval route.

## Supported operator commands

Use the authenticated socket/token configuration in
[owner-cli.md](owner-cli.md#connection-and-authentication) and the existing online
owner provisioning in [web-research-broker-core.md](web-research-broker-core.md).
From the built candidate, inspect and retain identities before preparing a trial:

```zsh
node dist/cli.js research-trial runtime --json > research-runtime.json
node dist/cli.js research-policy list --json > research-policies.json
```

Supply the externally approved definition in `trial.json`. Copy `artifactDigest`
from `research-runtime.json`'s `data` object, and ID/version/semantic hash from the
selected `research-policies.json` entry. Require the approved lexical policy,
all explicit resource limits, cohort identity and absolute deadline; do not replace
missing cohort approval with arbitrary example numbers. This JSON shape is the
strict API contract in `src/api/contract-research-policies.ts` and is exercised by
`src/api/research-trials.test.ts`.

```zsh
node dist/cli.js research-trial prepare --definition-file trial.json --command-id trial-prepare --json
trial_id="$(node -p 'JSON.parse(require("node:fs").readFileSync("trial.json", "utf8")).trialId')"
node dist/cli.js research-trial export "$trial_id" --json > trial-before.json
```

Expected: preparation completes and export has `taskId: null`, the exact policy
and zero usage. Retain the definition and command/client IDs. Any mismatch or
rejection stops admission. Start through `research-trial start`, supplying the
project ID from the browser's project URL, approved preset IDs from the owner's
workflow catalog, and a UTF-8 request file. Save the project ID as `project_id` and approved presets as `planner_preset_id`
and `implementer_preset_id` in the operator shell; these identities must come from
that owner's project URL/catalog. Save the approved task text as `request.txt`.
Then run:

```zsh
node dist/cli.js research-trial start "$trial_id" --project-id "$project_id" --request-file request.txt --planner-preset-id "$planner_preset_id" --implementer-preset-id "$implementer_preset_id" --base main --json
```

Use the frozen base/reasoning choices when they differ. The command's help lists every field:

```zsh
node dist/cli.js research-trial start --help
```

`start` sends ordinary `workflow.start` with the prepared `workflowCommandId`.
An explicit conflicting `--command-id` is rejected. Its existing immutable
planner/implementer model/reasoning/prompt assignment remains authoritative.
The browser's ordinary New task action does not implicitly opt into trials.
After starting, `research-trial export` must show the bound task ID and original
policy. Subsequent calls update the same aggregate and role counters.

The authenticated API equivalents are `GET /api/v1/research-trials/runtime`,
`GET /api/v1/research-trials/:trialId`, and the existing `POST /api/v1/commands`
with `type: "research_trial.prepare"`. CLI JSON schema 3 adds strict runtime/export
kinds; existing task/session projections and their API minor remain unchanged.

## Export, handoff and recovery

Export includes the frozen policy/hash, runtime-match state, conservative `usage`,
confirmed `observedWork`, `uncertainMaximum`, uncertain-reservation count, role
usage, and each call's request digest, timing, outcome and attributed work.
Terminal compact evidence includes core/owner artifact and policy identities,
configured/effective lexical ranker, cache disposition, budget and aggregate
snapshot at completion. Explicit continuations do not claim a ranker execution.
Fallback/mixed-selection counts are zero; no fallback is enabled. An unfinished
call has `evidence: null`. Historical work is explicitly unavailable, not zero.

Pi evidence and compact trial evidence commit atomically. Raw queries, full result
collections, pages, chunk text and handles are excluded from these records. The
existing bounded first-search-result summary is preserved. Planner-selected
handoff material remains the explicit, separate immutable Plan artifact described
in [planner-research-handoff.md](planner-research-handoff.md). `inheritedVisibility`
identifies its planner origin, implementer consumer and consumption status without
copying its text. Reuse costs no call; independent implementer research is charged
to that role. Export is research evidence, not hidden scoring or solution-exposure
attestation.

Restart the owner using its existing service/recovery procedure with the same
state root and frozen runtime. Inspect export, then use ordinary session reopen
when needed. Do not delete the database, modify reservations, assign a new trial,
or change the frozen artifact to recover budget. Changed artifacts require the
original admitted runtime or a separately authorized new cohort. A schema-34
migration failure retains the normal pre-migration backup; follow
[tracked-task-storage-and-recovery.md](tracked-task-storage-and-recovery.md).
Rolling back a database loses later work and cannot resume the same trial safely.

# Architecture Heuristics

This document records accepted, cross-cutting decision guidance for RelayView.
Heuristics are defaults for evaluating new designs; they are neither domain
vocabulary nor claims that a behavior has been implemented. A design may depart
from a heuristic when it records the concrete invariant, limitation, or evidence
that requires the exception. A consequential, hard-to-reverse exception may
also require an architecture decision record.

Verified current behavior remains documented in the relevant authoritative
subsystem contract. Specific consequential decisions and their tradeoffs remain
documented in `docs/authoritative/adr/`. The form those documents take — present
tense, contract rather than changelog, and which issue references are retained —
is governed by [authoritative documentation standards](authoritative-documentation-standards.md),
not by a heuristic here. The accepted owner decisions below are one of the
reference categories that document retains.

## Optimize For Human Attention And Direction

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-19: treat human attention and direction as the
scarce resources in agent-assisted development. RelayView's objective is to turn
human intent into verified, useful outcomes with less supervision and decision
overhead. Producing more code is not sufficient evidence of progress toward that
objective.

Use clear contracts, deterministic tools, and admitted automated validation and
review to handle work that otherwise demands repeated human checking and
correction. Preserve human direction over goals, scope, consequential tradeoffs,
and acceptance. Make intervention useful: present the decision needed, the
relevant evidence, uncertainty, and consequences without requiring the person
to reconstruct the execution history. Routine coordination and repeated
explanations should not consume attention that the system can conserve.

The existing [automated review workflow](planner-review-rounds.md) and the planned
Human Review Brief serve this objective through different responsibilities:
automated review can identify defects before Human review, while the brief is
intended to organize the exact candidate, checks, unresolved concerns, and
decision context for efficient inspection. The brief remains roadmap work;
neither mechanism's existence proves a reduction in human effort.

Evaluate active supervision and review time, avoidable interruptions, repeated
instructions, decision quality, and subsequent rework alongside coding outcomes,
latency, and resource use. Preserve visibility of uncertainty and required
acceptance boundaries while reducing burden. The
[human-decision hypothesis](../speculative/relayview-theory-of-effectiveness.md#h6-inspectable-evidence-can-improve-human-decisions-if-it-reduces-review-burden)
records the expected benefit and evidence limits. This is a product design
priority, not a claim that model capability, correctness, or compute constraints
have ceased to matter.

### Design For Sustained Work Between Human Checkpoints

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-20: design RelayView for long periods of useful
work without routine human input, including overnight runs. Preconfiguration
enables unattended execution, which serves the broader objective of conserving
human attention. This principle applies across Community and Teams.

Owner decision, accepted 2026-10-04: concentrate necessary Human interaction
into deliberate checkpoints that unlock the longest safe interval of independent
work. Ask foreseeable questions as soon as there is enough evidence to answer
them reliably, and collect related questions, setup steps, and requests for new
authority into one useful checkpoint. Optimize the number and timing of
interruptions as well as total Human effort. Do not ask speculative questions
that the workflow can resolve within its existing authority merely to make a
checkpoint look complete.

Move foreseeable configuration and authorization decisions before execution.
Let users establish task direction, acceptance criteria, supported capabilities,
dependency sources, external-service access, credential bindings, and resource
limits upfront. Within that configured authority, design routine acquisition,
builds, tests, coordination, and bounded recovery to proceed without repeated
user confirmation. Surface detectable missing prerequisites before a run so
users can resolve them while preparing the work.

An agent-ready assignment has no known unresolved consequential choice that
would predictably stop implementation. Task preparation should expose such
choices while a Human is already defining the work; readiness does not promise
that unexpected questions will never arise. Collaborative task preparation and
unattended implementation are separate interactions. Their overlap lets a Human
shape future tasks while ready tasks continue through owner-controlled roles.

When execution encounters a consequential decision, missing configuration, or a
need for new authority, preserve progress and continue independent authorized
work where possible. Before interrupting the Human, examine other foreseeable
decisions needed to resume useful work and present the related questions together
with their evidence, options, and consequences. Leave a clear account of any
remaining blocker; do not invent permission or count blocked verification as
passed. Prepare results and verification evidence for human inspection, manual
testing, acceptance, and further direction.

The first safe opportunity to interact with an exact implementation candidate
is another useful Human checkpoint. Make that candidate inspectable and, where
practical, manually testable so the Human can discover defects or differences
from their intent before merge. Formal approval still follows the required
current verification and review evidence, and applies only to the candidate
actually inspected. A changed candidate needs fresh applicable evidence and a
fresh Human decision. This checkpoint is part of conserving attention:
discovering an intent mismatch before merge avoids a later interruption and
repair cycle.

Make the review package especially usable for intermediate changes whose value
is not obvious from a visible feature. Explain why the change matters, identify
the exact candidate, and separate what current deterministic checks establish
from what they cannot assess. A bounded contract with enumerable inputs and
outputs may have strong automated coverage and little value in repeating the
same calls by hand. Interface clarity, visual layout, discoverability, and fit
to Human intent often need direct inspection even when focused browser tests
pass; expanding brittle browser assertions cannot exhaust those judgments.

State the remaining Human review need explicitly. When direct exercise can
resolve it, give the shortest repeatable setup, action, and expected observation
for the exact candidate. When manual testing adds little, say why the automated
evidence is a suitable basis for the Human's decision and name its limits; do
not create busywork to fill a checklist. When useful manual testing is
impractical, explain the constraint without implying that the Human exercised
the behavior. Human acceptance remains necessary in every case, and neither
automated coverage nor a successful manual check is proof beyond its stated
scope.

The [work-between-checkpoints hypothesis](../speculative/relayview-teams-business-plan.md#market-hypotheses-not-decisions-or-established-evidence)
illustrates the intended rhythm: refine tasks and set clear directions in the
afternoon, let agents work overnight, then manually test, verify, and redirect in
the morning. That schedule is an example, not a requirement. Supporting sustained
unattended work is accepted design guidance; whether this rhythm reduces total
human effort remains a hypothesis, and this principle does not establish that
every supporting capability is implemented.

## Build For The Only Installation That Exists

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-19: RelayView has no release and no installation
other than the development host. Do not add compatibility for earlier versions of
this project's own code. When a change alters a contract, change it, and require
the older participant to be rebuilt or relaunched.

Distinguish durable artifacts from live participants, because the project's
genuine care about history is what makes this mistake easy. Sessions, events,
commands, plans, candidates, and audit records are evidence. They must remain
readable with their original semantics, and reinterpreting them would falsify the
record. That is history integrity, not backward compatibility, and this heuristic
does not weaken it.

Everything a running process holds may change outright: protocol shapes, tool
schemas, extension code, prompts, configuration, and any read model that can be
rebuilt from durable records.

Apply it as follows. When a change tempts you to add a compatibility path, name
the artifact that requires it. If it is a durable record, keep the record
readable and say so in the contract. If it is a running process, the answer is
to relaunch it. If it is a deployment that does not exist, do not write the
code. Symptoms worth catching in review: an alias normalizing a superseded
name, an operation accepting two input shapes, a branch keyed on a build that
only ever ran here, a migration for data no installation holds, and failure
text explaining a shape nothing sends.

Revisit this heuristic when a first release exists. Until then the cost is
concrete and recurring: every compatibility seam must be reconsidered by every
later change that touches the same contract.

## Use The Right Tool For The Job

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-19: choose a mechanism because it fits the
required capability and constraints. Evaluate correctness, coverage, reliability,
authority, integration fit, and total execution and maintenance cost. Familiarity,
availability, or an agent's ability to attempt the work is insufficient by itself.

The [deterministic-systems preference](#prefer-deterministic-systems-wherever-they-can-do-the-work)
is RelayView's concrete application of this general maxim: consider integration
with existing software, then internal deterministic solutions, then agentic
solutions for the remaining work. The maxim explains that ordering rather than
replacing it with an unconstrained choice. Apply it to each part of a capability;
a combination of mechanisms may fit the job best. Record the concrete limitation
or evidence that justifies departing from the default.

## Treat Agents As Contractors Working Against Verifiable Contracts

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-19: treat agents as untrusted contractors with
clear assignments and verifiable acceptance criteria. Here, untrusted describes
an authority boundary, not an assumption of dishonesty. Agents can misunderstand
requirements, overlook defects, or sincerely report completion before the work
satisfies its contract.

Give an agent a clear contract for what done means: the intended outcome, scope,
constraints, and observable acceptance criteria. Treat its completion report as
a submitted candidate for validation. Check the exact version it reports against
that contract using attributable evidence, and return concrete unmet requirements
through the admitted feedback and correction workflow. Changed candidates need
current evidence; a report or approval for an earlier version cannot establish
that a later version meets the contract.

Use the [deterministic-systems default](#prefer-deterministic-systems-wherever-they-can-do-the-work)
to perform checks wherever suitable tools exist, with agent review for remaining
context-sensitive judgments. Evaluate whether the checks cover the intended
behavior: successful execution of inadequate checks does not establish contract
satisfaction. Make requirement changes explicit rather than silently relaxing
the contract to fit the submitted work. Keep agent claims, observed validation,
review judgments, and Human acceptance distinct.

This principle explains the separation between
[implementation reports](implementer-implementation-reports.md),
[validation evidence](repository-validation-manifest.md), and
[review and feedback](planner-review-rounds.md). It does not grant an agent
acceptance authority, introduce an additional reviewer, or change admitted
correction budgets or ablation configurations. The benefit of a particular
feedback mechanism remains subject to evaluation.

## Prefer Deterministic Systems Wherever They Can Do The Work

Owner decision, accepted 2026-09-19: use deterministic systems wherever they can
adequately perform the required work. This default includes analysis and decision
procedures, as well as data management and execution bookkeeping. An agent's
ability to perform a task is not itself a reason to allocate inference to it.

# Current Orchestration Architecture

## Scope

This document describes the behavior implemented by the current TypeScript scaffold. Proposed multi-agent tracking and control behavior is documented separately in [../speculative/multi-agent-observability-and-control.md](../speculative/multi-agent-observability-and-control.md).

The bounded SQLite backup-retention contract is documented in [tracked task storage and recovery](tracked-task-storage-and-recovery.md). Startup conservatively adopts verified historical automatic snapshots, protects the exact recorded recovery point, prunes only revalidated redundant bundles, and exposes bounded path-free status plus an owner-local dry-run plan. Automatic creation and historical cleanup share the same deterministic planner and crash-safe mutation boundary.

Cross-cutting default decision rules live in [Architecture Heuristics](architecture-heuristics.md). They guide new designs but do not themselves claim that behavior is implemented.
The [task archive aggregate storage](task-archive-storage.md) persists a
role-neutral task retirement checkpoint, bounded API read projections, and
authenticated `task.archive` and `task.abandon` commands. Client controls and
navigation views remain proposed.
The [successor task lifecycle core](successor-task-lifecycle.md) persists an
internal merge-gated state machine and exact terminal release proof; its
provider/local-Git integration and public Human-review controls remain proposed.
The [external CI adapter boundary](external-ci-adapter.md) stores revisioned
project bindings and provides owner-private Gitea Actions observation for the
internal version-2 validation evidence contract.
The [remote hosting adapter boundary](remote-hosting-adapter.md) defines internal
repository/ref identity, Gitea observation, and guarded publication semantics;
revisioned owner bindings and sanitized client configuration are connected,
and owner-controlled publication verifies the exact candidate through a
durable intent.
The [pull-request adapter boundary](pull-request-adapter.md) defines separate
project admission, authenticated Gitea PR and review observation, a
policy-required draft effect, and exact-head internal merge recovery.
Agent instruction authoring follows the accepted default of
[positive action language](architecture-heuristics.md#use-positive-action-language-for-agent-instructions).
Authorization and disclosure restrictions follow
[external enforcement boundaries](architecture-heuristics.md#enforce-prohibitions-outside-the-agent),
independently of model compliance with prompt prohibitions.
Tool-call contracts follow
[minimized required model transcription](architecture-heuristics.md#minimize-required-model-transcription),
resolving owner-held canonical fields from storage instead of requiring the
model to reproduce them.

## Focused Chat And Agent Publications

New focused Chat sessions use the [durable status fallback](focused-chat-status-fallback.md): natural status publications reset a tiered owner timer, and an owner request enters only an already-running Pi model boundary. Timers cannot wake agents or create Human review influence.

Focused Chat provides a retained-history focused-conversation projection and
route-addressable Implementer Chat. New task-bound Planner, Implementer, and
Reviewer Chat use an owner-mediated, non-interrupting inbox and the private
`publish_focused_chat_message` tool rather than transcript inference. Exact
user messages and explicit agent publications are durable events in the existing
owner ledger; private prompts, reasoning, tools, protocol traffic, reports, and
telemetry remain in Dashboard. New roles use focused transport v6 with [natural acknowledgements](natural-agent-acknowledgements.md). Implementers and Plan reviewers retain v5 delivery:
active inboxes reach Pi after the current tool batch through native streaming
steer, preserving the active tool and agent loop. Admission requires the matching
Pi user-message event, rather than the RPC queue acknowledgement. Pre-v5
Implementer/Reviewer transports and current Planner transports keep the owner's
settlement-aware turn queue. Idle delivery starts a normal prompt. See the
[Implementer delivery contract](implementer-communication-context.md) and
[Reviewer conversation/judgment contract](reviewer-communication-context.md).
A timed-out or restart-interrupted admission is failed closed as
delivery-ambiguous and is never automatically redelivered. Retained sessions
without the focused-transport assignment marker remain readable through the
compatibility projection. Both communication-context ablation arms
receive identical tool, prompt, inbox, publication, and replay semantics.
Eligible task-bound roles must emit a brief, human-friendly, uncorrelated
`progress` publication when they complete one meaningful internal work phase and
begin the next, so later Human inspection reveals both the completed result and
current direction. The guidance suppresses routine tool/file/check narration and
owner-visible workflow boundaries; answers and
acknowledgements remain correlated to admitted inbox messages. They may also emit
a concise uncorrelated `question` before the Human opens Chat; it never creates a
workflow wait state, and any correlated publication must copy an admitted inbox
identity. Durable owner
workflow events, rather than model prose, present known lifecycle boundaries.
The enabled guidance applies to Planner discussion and complete Plan
production for newly admitted ordinary Planners and the explicit enabled
benchmark arm; the explicit disabled arm and older benchmark versions remain
untreated. The persisted session relation controls prompt reconstruction after
restart. Planner-led Chat remains transcript-backed through the first durable
Plan finalization and becomes explicit-publication-only at that event; automatic
Planner Chat is explicit from task start and accepts owner/API inbox messages
during planning. Session history loads include task-level Plan events; a trusted
finalized-Plan summary fails safe to explicit projection when the bounded history
does not contain the transition event. Plan v1 remains the immutable implementation authority, and
post-finalization publication cannot revise it or replace replan.

## Planner Task Liaison

The [Planner Task-Liaison Contract](planner-task-liaison.md) and
[ADR 0011](adr/0011-keep-original-planner-as-task-liaison.md) are accepted. For newly
created tasks with an explicit liaison relation, the original planner session
remains the durable user-facing liaison independently of current Plan authority,
runtime ownership, and workflow phase. Legacy tasks remain unmarked. Passive
liaison conversation is non-authoritative; every replan, intervention, cancellation,
recovery, selection, integration, override, and Human completion decision stays
a distinct owner-authorized transition. Both workflow modes retain the same
liaison identity: discussion-first tasks keep their implementation-request gate,
while automatic tasks retain their creation-time authorization and
Dashboard-first initial destination. The responsibility's defining functional
capability is a relation-authorized set of bounded, sanitized,
freshness-aware read-only tools for changing task and visible-agent state. Those
tools let the liaison answer process questions without messaging or running the
other agents. The durable relation is stored in schema 48 and projected at API minor 28. Its observation tool and guidance activate in the same session
only after owner acceptance of Plan v1; initial planning does not see them.
See [Original Planner Task Observation](planner-task-observation.md).
Terminal historical questions use continuing conversation and idempotent
same-session activation. That conversation-only lifecycle is preserved for owner-proved unmarked retained original
Planner Chat through its stored assignment's compatibility controls, without
creating liaison identity, upgrading its transport, or granting liaison-only
capabilities. The same Planner Chat and Dashboard serve automatic and
planner-led tasks, including retained automatic history. Initial automatic
navigation stays Dashboard-first and tab navigation never changes workflow
authorization. Message controls retain owner lifecycle and assignment semantics;
terminal conversation activation is implemented in
[Terminal Planner Chat](terminal-planner-chat.md). The browser presents [owner progress context and status cards](planner-task-progress.md).
The liaison journey is covered by [integrated verification](planner-liaison-verification.md).
A default-home change is declined and mediated liaison actions are deferred to
speculative UI work; existing navigation and explicit controls remain the baseline. The browser implements
[planner-first sidebar ordering and bounded paging](workspace-sidebar-navigation.md)
from existing task/Plan relationships, without inferring liaison identity.
For a marked admitted planner, the existing private
`publish_focused_chat_message` tool is the liaison's planner-to-Human mechanism:
explicit answers, acknowledgements, meaningful progress, and nonblocking
questions become durable focused-Chat publication events while remaining
presentation-only. The persisted role remains `planner`; this tool fulfills the
planner's task-liaison responsibility rather than defining a new role. No second
liaison message channel is introduced.

content.text:
`ResearchEngine` is a lower-level **trusted** primitive. It does not authorize
callers or reserve logical calls. The service and compatibility broker provide
those responsibilities. Do not expose its context argument or provider/cache
constructors as agent tools. Only the trusted Brave constructor receives a search
credential; the package reads no model-provider credentials or environment config.
The host owns credential provisioning, process sandboxing and filesystem access.

## Work reservations, replay and lifecycle

Work contract version 1 distinguishes `calls`, `providerAttempts`,
`fetchedDocuments`, `fetchedBytes`, `scoringPairs`, `scoringWindows`,
`scoringTokens` and `elapsedMs`. `WorkScope.run` reserves a bounded maximum before
an effect, then reconciles actual successful use. Missing counters are `null`,
not fabricated zeroes, and work requiring an unavailable dimension is refused.
Effects that fail, are cancelled, or have uncertain outcomes retain their full
reservation conservatively until a known reconciliation completes. A reservation
may commit after the caller stops waiting; cancellation never starts its effect
late or assumes that its charge was rolled back. Reconciliation is idempotent,
never exceeds the original reservation, and cannot release another effect's charge.

The reference `VolatileWorkLedger` atomically enforces the whole shared allowance
in one JS process. Logical reservations capture their own post-decision snapshot,
so out-of-order completion does not change reported admission telemetry. The
service reserves one call and its whole deadline before request validation/cache
lookup/network activity, after host authorization. Transport-envelope rejection,
changed-ID replay, pre-cancellation, offline host denial and exhausted admission
do not start work. An authorized service whose engine is offline can return an
ordinary charged offline failure; the host should deny offline work at admission.

A physical search miss reserves one provider attempt. If reservation is denied,
the provider is never invoked and evidence reports no provider attempt or
provider failure. An invoked provider that fails still reports its failed attempt.
Cache hits and coalesced waiters reserve separate logical calls but no extra provider attempts. The shared
attempt belongs to its initiating scope; its cancellation follows the shared
flight's final waiter, even if the initiating caller cancels. Namespace, provider,
query/options and exact policy separate cache keys and flights. The legacy
adapter omits the new namespace and preserves existing cache-key bytes.

A fetch reserves one document and its maximum decoded body bytes, then reconciles
the successful body's actual length. Failure retains the maximum; these are
bounded decoded-body accounting units, **not** network packet/wire-byte meters.
Redirects remain within the existing three-hop, public-address and deadline
boundary. `providerAttempts` counts search-provider invocations, not document
redirect hops. The core performs no automatic retries. Trusted future composite operations
must give each retry/fan-out effect its own reservation; tests cover that seam.

Lexical scoring reserves chunk-count times normalized focus-term-count pairs;
window/token inference counts are zero because this release does no tokenization
or neural inference. Elapsed work reserves the per-call deadline, reconciles
observed execution time before the final accounting acknowledgement. Final call
accounting and evidence acknowledgement latency is excluded from this counter; both waits
still obey the original operation deadline. Cancellation/uncertainty before
reconciliation retains the maximum until a known reconciliation completes.
Cancellation during evidence persistence does not undo already reconciled work.
This is summed execution wall time, not CPU time; concurrent calls reserve
independently. Hosts provide a consistent clock and declare exact policy limits.
No benchmark numeric policy is invented here.

`SupervisedRanker` defines explicit identity/version, result-count, positive-match
policy, source-index tie breaks, lexical fallback, work estimation and a bounded
signal-aware selection call for later prototypes. Only the pinned lexical
implementation is executed by this release. Future workers, fallback selection
and new ranking behavior require separate admission and release identities.

Replay results and document handles are transient. The service retains at most
4,096 call results, each bounded to 128 KiB, until close; ordinary host limits can
be much lower. `close()` aborts active calls and rejects later execution. Host,
caller and service cancellation are checked before replay, including completed
results; cancelled replays cannot return cached success. Each pending replay also
observes its own caller signal while waiting. Cancelling that wait returns timeout
without cancelling the original execution, altering its retained result, charging
another call or writing another evidence record. The initiating caller still owns
the execution lifetime. The engine retains at most 64 documents for ten minutes,
bound to session, capability, policy and namespace. Four initial chunks, three explicit continuation chunks,
eight continuations, 120 KiB cumulative document-visible bytes and restart loss
remain the [four-chunk release contract](four-chunk-lexical-release.md).

**The reference host is not restart-safe.** A new volatile ledger starts a new
allowance and must not be represented as recovery. Reusing the same ledger across
replacement services conserves budget and refuses already-reserved effect IDs;
it does not reconstruct old results. Durable hosts must persist reservations,
reconciliation and replay disposition atomically and fail closed on uncertain
execution. Merely labelling a custom ledger `durable` proves nothing. The
[owner research trial allowances](owner-research-trials.md) contract owns the
production implementation and restart verification of that behavior.

Authorization, ledger reservation/reconciliation and evidence hooks receive the
call's combined abort signal. The service bounds all asynchronous host waits by
the same caller/host/service cancellation and operation deadline. Hosts should
cooperate with that signal; the core cannot undo an external write or charge.
Late completions cannot resume work or change a terminal timeout into success.

The evidence sink receives only canonical compact evidence, request digest and
release identity, without queries, bodies, handles or chunks. Call accounting must
acknowledge reconciliation before the service submits success evidence. A failed
reconciliation submits failure evidence while the lifetime remains active; a
cancelled or expired reconciliation submits no new evidence. A sink failure
returns `unavailable` and its terminal failure is retained on replay without
repeating effects. Cancellation or deadline expiry returns `timeout` and starts
no new evidence write. A write already in flight may still commit; its uncertain
disposition is never overwritten or retried automatically, and replay retains
the failure. There is no automatic sink retry or success claim. Retain host
diagnostics and repair/reconcile the sink before admitting replacement execution.

### Cancellation and physical activity

Abort-raced research results remain prompt cancellation outcomes; they do not prove that their underlying effect stopped. Internally, `ResearchActivity` uses Node async context to retain promises hidden by those races. Supervised owner tools and broker requests drain this activity before publishing quiescence. Search flights have their own activity scope so every coalesced waiter retains the shared physical work. Transport tracking includes DNS completion and the HTTPS request's `close` event. This does not assert rollback of an already transmitted provider request or charge; uncertain work reservations remain charged. Standalone result and cancellation contracts are unchanged.

## Package and verification

The package supports the repository Node ranges (22.19–22.x and 24.11–24.x), uses
ES modules and exact-pins parse5 8.0.1, saxes 6.0.0 and pdfjs-dist 6.3.289 with an
independent lockfile. pdfjs-dist text extraction is pure JavaScript; its optional
`@napi-rs/canvas` native dependency installs per-platform from the same lockfile
for rendering the package never performs, so the sandboxed broker loads no native
addon on the extraction path. PDF extraction runs the pdf.js legacy build inside a
dedicated worker thread with an owned stream-expansion pre-scan, page and output
ceilings, a wall-clock watchdog, a capped worker heap, and the shared fetch
deadline; a policy admits it only through the `pdfExtraction` value.
Linux x64 on Node 22.19.0 is the verified platform here. Other platforms have no
new execution evidence; production Bubblewrap isolation remains Linux-specific.
The package has no SQLite dependency. `fixture.ts` supplies a
credential-free trusted host and fake pinned DNS/HTTPS source.

From the repository root:

```zsh
npm ci
npm run build --prefix src/research/core
npm run fixture --prefix src/research/core
npm run artifact --prefix src/research/core
npx vitest run src/research --maxWorkers=4
node test/replay-three-chunk-baseline.mjs > /tmp/relayview-three-chunk-replay.json
npm run typecheck
npm run build
```

Expected: all commands exit zero. The standalone fixture reports four initial
chunks, three continuation chunks, two calls, one fetched document, 702 decoded
bytes, no provider attempt and `durability: volatile`. The artifact command emits
SHA-256 identities covering compiled JS/types, manifest, lockfile and the identity
script. It contains no timestamps or credentials. `golden.json` freezes complete
fetch values from pre-extraction commit `695727f`, replacing only random handles
with `opaque`. Tests compare default/focused/no-match output byte-for-byte in
structure, including IDs/order/digests and exact visible-byte accounting.
Historical three-chunk replay still checks its original complete JSON/Markdown;
its helper copies the moved supporting primitives without changing frozen
chunker code, evidence or expected results.

Run the repository validation manifest's `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`,
`npm run test:showcase`, `npm run test:workflow` and `git diff --check` as well.
Existing transport suites cover SSRF, redirect/DNS/peer validation, decompression,
size/deadline/cancellation and credential redaction through the shared modules.
The standalone tests cover host denial, strict requests, composite work ceilings,
concurrent aggregate admission/replay, cache/coalescing, cancellation, sink failure,
blocked authorization/accounting/evidence hooks and late completions, cancelled
completed and pending replay, accounting-before-evidence ordering and failure,
provider-reservation denial versus invoked-provider failure,
no cross-session/policy/namespace/capability handles and transient restart loss.

To build a portable tarball in a disposable output directory:

```zsh
core_package_output="$(mktemp -d /tmp/relayview-core-package-XXXXXX)"
(cd src/research/core && npm pack --pack-destination "$core_package_output")
```

Expected: `relayview-research-core-1.2.0.tgz` is created. Retain its SHA-256 and
`npm run artifact --prefix src/research/core` output with the candidate commit.
To verify the packed artifact outside the source tree, continue in the same shell:

```zsh

`ResearchEngine` is a lower-level **trusted** primitive. It does not authorize
callers or reserve logical calls. The service and compatibility broker provide
those responsibilities. Do not expose its context argument or provider/cache
constructors as agent tools. Only the trusted Brave constructor receives a search
credential; the package reads no model-provider credentials or environment config.
The host owns credential provisioning, process sandboxing and filesystem access.

## Work reservations, replay and lifecycle

Work contract version 1 distinguishes `calls`, `providerAttempts`,
`fetchedDocuments`, `fetchedBytes`, `scoringPairs`, `scoringWindows`,
`scoringTokens` and `elapsedMs`. `WorkScope.run` reserves a bounded maximum before
an effect, then reconciles actual successful use. Missing counters are `null`,
not fabricated zeroes, and work requiring an unavailable dimension is refused.
Effects that fail, are cancelled, or have uncertain outcomes retain their full
reservation conservatively until a known reconciliation completes. A reservation
may commit after the caller stops waiting; cancellation never starts its effect
late or assumes that its charge was rolled back. Reconciliation is idempotent,
never exceeds the original reservation, and cannot release another effect's charge.

The reference `VolatileWorkLedger` atomically enforces the whole shared allowance
in one JS process. Logical reservations capture their own post-decision snapshot,
so out-of-order completion does not change reported admission telemetry. The
service reserves one call and its whole deadline before request validation/cache
lookup/network activity, after host authorization. Transport-envelope rejection,
changed-ID replay, pre-cancellation, offline host denial and exhausted admission
do not start work. An authorized service whose engine is offline can return an
ordinary charged offline failure; the host should deny offline work at admission.

A physical search miss reserves one provider attempt. If reservation is denied,
the provider is never invoked and evidence reports no provider attempt or
provider failure. An invoked provider that fails still reports its failed attempt.
Cache hits and coalesced waiters reserve separate logical calls but no extra provider attempts. The shared
attempt belongs to its initiating scope; its cancellation follows the shared
flight's final waiter, even if the initiating caller cancels. Namespace, provider,
query/options and exact policy separate cache keys and flights. The legacy
adapter omits the new namespace and preserves existing cache-key bytes.

A fetch reserves one document and its maximum decoded body bytes, then reconciles
the successful body's actual length. Failure retains the maximum; these are
bounded decoded-body accounting units, **not** network packet/wire-byte meters.
Redirects remain within the existing three-hop, public-address and deadline
boundary. `providerAttempts` counts search-provider invocations, not document
redirect hops. The core performs no automatic retries. Trusted future composite operations
must give each retry/fan-out effect its own reservation; tests cover that seam.

Lexical scoring reserves chunk-count times normalized focus-term-count pairs;
window/token inference counts are zero because this release does no tokenization
or neural inference. Elapsed work reserves the per-call deadline, reconciles
observed execution time before the final accounting acknowledgement. Final call
accounting and evidence acknowledgement latency is excluded from this counter; both waits
still obey the original operation deadline. Cancellation/uncertainty before
reconciliation retains the maximum until a known reconciliation completes.
Cancellation during evidence persistence does not undo already reconciled work.
This is summed execution wall time, not CPU time; concurrent calls reserve
independently. Hosts provide a consistent clock and declare exact policy limits.
No benchmark numeric policy is invented here.

`SupervisedRanker` defines explicit identity/version, result-count, positive-match
policy, source-index tie breaks, lexical fallback, work estimation and a bounded
signal-aware selection call for later prototypes. Only the pinned lexical
implementation is executed by this release. Future workers, fallback selection
and new ranking behavior require separate admission and release identities.

Replay results and document handles are transient. The service retains at most
4,096 call results, each bounded to 128 KiB, until close; ordinary host limits can
be much lower. `close()` aborts active calls and rejects later execution. Host,
caller and service cancellation are checked before replay, including completed
results; cancelled replays cannot return cached success. Each pending replay also
observes its own caller signal while waiting. Cancelling that wait returns timeout
without cancelling the original execution, altering its retained result, charging
another call or writing another evidence record. The initiating caller still owns
the execution lifetime. The engine retains at most 64 documents for ten minutes,
bound to session, capability, policy and namespace. Four initial chunks, three explicit continuation chunks,
eight continuations, 120 KiB cumulative document-visible bytes and restart loss
remain the [four-chunk release contract](four-chunk-lexical-release.md).

**The reference host is not restart-safe.** A new volatile ledger starts a new
allowance and must not be represented as recovery. Reusing the same ledger across
replacement services conserves budget and refuses already-reserved effect IDs;
it does not reconstruct old results. Durable hosts must persist reservations,
reconciliation and replay disposition atomically and fail closed on uncertain
execution. Merely labelling a custom ledger `durable` proves nothing. The
[owner research trial allowances](owner-research-trials.md) contract owns the
production implementation and restart verification of that behavior.

Authorization, ledger reservation/reconciliation and evidence hooks receive the
call's combined abort signal. The service bounds all asynchronous host waits by
the same caller/host/service cancellation and operation deadline. Hosts should
cooperate with that signal; the core cannot undo an external write or charge.
Late completions cannot resume work or change a terminal timeout into success.

The evidence sink receives only canonical compact evidence, request digest and
release identity, without queries, bodies, handles or chunks. Call accounting must
acknowledge reconciliation before the service submits success evidence. A failed
reconciliation submits failure evidence while the lifetime remains active; a
cancelled or expired reconciliation submits no new evidence. A sink failure
returns `unavailable` and its terminal failure is retained on replay without
repeating effects. Cancellation or deadline expiry returns `timeout` and starts
no new evidence write. A write already in flight may still commit; its uncertain
disposition is never overwritten or retried automatically, and replay retains
the failure. There is no automatic sink retry or success claim. Retain host
diagnostics and repair/reconcile the sink before admitting replacement execution.

Abort-raced research results remain prompt cancellation outcomes; they do not prove that their underlying effect stopped. Internally, `ResearchActivity` uses Node async context to retain promises hidden by those races. Supervised owner tools and broker requests drain this activity before publishing quiescence. # RelayView research MCP 1.1.0

Thin MCP stdio bridge and supervised Unix-socket service over the shared
`@relayview/research-core` 1.1.0 source, selection `lexical-v2-initial-4`.
The tarball includes that exact compiled source, parse5 8.0.1 and saxes 6.0.0
through its shrinkwrap. It does not contain a second ranker or import the owner.

Use Node 22.19–22.x or 24.11–24.x on Linux. Build with `npm run build`, inspect
`npm run artifact`, and pack with `npm pack`. Run the credential-free transport
check with `node dist/mcp/smoke.js` (requires Bubblewrap). The fixture calls a
supervised service through a network-disabled stdio bridge.

With no source option, the launcher derives `public-web-v1` and GitHub remains
allowed. Add `--github-excluded` to derive `github-excluded-v1`. Readiness reports
both the requested profile and its complete effective descriptor; duplicated,
unknown, or requested/effective mismatches fail startup.

Trusted launch: `node dist/mcp/main.js --directory /absolute/private/trial-dir`.
Supply the version-1 trusted session/policy/limits JSON over inherited descriptor
3 and the Brave credential over inherited descriptor 4, then close both writers.
Neither value is accepted over MCP, argv, or ordinary environment variables.
For an explicitly disposable fixture, add `--fixture` before `--directory`.
For the GitHub-excluded profile, add `--github-excluded` before `--directory`.

Client command: `node dist/mcp/bridge.js /absolute/private/trial-dir/research.sock`.
Only `web_search` and `web_fetch` are exposed. Core requests, canonical results,
accounting and private-address rules retain their shared meaning. Responses have
one JSON text block and no `structuredContent` duplicate.

The private socket mount is the session capability. The trusted supervisor must
isolate each trial's filesystem/mount namespace, prevent agent edits to client
configuration and binaries, and hide all other session sockets, credential and
control paths. A same-UID unrestricted shell is outside that boundary. Do not
present socket file modes as protection from the same unrestricted user.

This standalone host uses volatile accounting and keeps a `started` marker.
Bridge reconnect preserves the live service allowance. Service restart in the
same directory is refused; do not delete the marker to resume a trial. Durable
benchmark provisioning/accounting is separate integration work. Stop the whole
trial on sidecar loss; only a newly authorized trial may receive fresh state.

The repository's `docs/authoritative/research-mcp.md` contains complete setup,
pinned native verification, live smoke, recovery, cleanup and evidence limits.
